Automated segmentation of myocardium in CMR images, which is faster than planimetry, yields an improved estimate of LV mass compared with planimetry.
automated segmentation of myocardial voxels that contain a mixture of blood and myocardium yields a 14-17% increase in LV mass compared with full voxel segmentation.

a new approach to the problem of segmentation of the heart in medical imaging.
the development of a new segmentation algorithm for the left ventricular mass quantification using partial voxel interpolation.
the development of a new method for the quantification of the left ventricular mass (LVM).

automated CMR segmentation can be used to account for myocardial partial voxals and that the resulting LVM quantification is accurate.

partial voxel interpolation can improve the accuracy of CMR-based LVM quantification, especially when the spatial resolution of the images is relatively low.
